title: Epistemic Damage Framework
abstract: We introduce a framework for analyzing and quantifying model-induced bias in scientific data evaluation. While experimental measurements remain unaffected by modeling choices, the interpretation of these measurements depends critically on the assumptions embedded in the model space. When these assumptions are violated or implicitly extended beyond their domain of validity, fitted parameters may appear consistent with the data while lacking physical meaning. In scattering analysis this becomes acute when scalar formulations are applied outside their symmetry class. We therefore treat epistemic damage as the spread, persistence, and downstream inferential effect of such model misuse.

thoughts.title: Scalar Reduction in Scattering
thoughts.problem: Vectorial amplitudes are often reduced to scalar forms outside their valid domain.
thoughts.impact: Structural inference becomes biased while the fit can still look numerically good.
thoughts.method: Compare scalar and vectorial pathways with independent evaluators.

thoughts.title: Multi-Path Evaluation
thoughts.core_statement: Independent routes should agree only when the assumptions agree.
thoughts.problem: A single fit pathway hides approximation error inside one hypothesis space.
thoughts.impact: Silent inconsistency becomes visible when PDD, Debye, FFT, and orientation averaging diverge.
thoughts.method: Run parallel scattering pathways against the same structural state.

thoughts.title: Epistemic Damage Index
thoughts.core_statement: Scientific impact is not just spread; it is spread weighted by error.
thoughts.problem: Citation count alone does not measure whether a reused model distorts later inference.
thoughts.impact: A widely propagated but invalid model can reshape the admissible interpretation space of a field.
thoughts.method: Score reach, severity, and persistence on a citation and assumption graph.

thoughts.title: Propagation Through Literature
thoughts.core_statement: The paper explains the system; the homepage exposes the system.
thoughts.problem: Misapplied models survive as defaults in papers, software, teaching, and protocols.
thoughts.impact: Downstream work inherits assumptions without revalidating them.
thoughts.method: Treat papers, software defaults, and educational standards as linked propagation nodes.

results.title: Symmetry limits can be stated as a reusable result.
results.summary: The homepage result layer should not restate the whole analysis. It should expose the outcome that scalar reduction is only admissible under explicit symmetry and shape assumptions, then link that claim back to the tracked publications where the constraint is visible.

results.title: Corrections remain part of the same literature object.
results.summary: The original capped-cylinder paper and its addendum belong to one tracked result chain. The result view should therefore link the corrected record directly to the original publication pair instead of treating correction as a separate analytical narrative.

results.title: Propagation can be followed beyond the seed pair.
results.summary: The literature task expands from the seed publication into downstream reuse. This result layer should therefore point from the curated claim to the concrete citing papers that carry the model into later SAXS and morphology work.

bibliography.title: Literature Research Bibliography
bibliography.intro: This closing bibliography keeps six papers that are most directly relevant to the capped-cylinder seed record and its immediate literature context.
bibliography.note: This closing section should read like a compact literature research record. It is reduced to the six most relevant papers linked to the seed paper and formatted so it can be copied out as a standalone bibliography draft.
bibliography.selection_note: Relevance is ranked from the seed paper outward: the seed papers first, then directly linked papers in the tracked graph, then papers reused across more result cards, and finally citation strength as a tie-breaker.
